parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem:
A and B react together to give product AB.
$$\text{A} + \text{B} \rightarrow \text{AB}$$

When the concentrations of A and B are both $0.0100\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$, the rate of formation of AB is $7.62 \times 10^{-4}\text{ mol dm}^{-3}\text{s}^{-1}$.

When the concentrations of A and B are both $0.0200\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$, the rate of formation of AB is $3.05 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol dm}^{-3}\text{s}^{-1}$.
parts.text: Complete the **three** possible rate equations that are consistent with these data.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Choose **one** of the rate equations you have written in (i), and calculate the value of the rate constant, $k$. Include the units of $k$.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Explain why it is **not** possible to calculate a value for the half-life, $t_{\frac{1}{2}}$, of this reaction using the value of the rate constant $k$ calculated in (ii) and the equation $k = 0.693/t_{\frac{1}{2}}$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: Catalysts may be homogeneous or heterogeneous.
parts.text: Identify **two** metals that act as heterogeneous catalysts in the removal of $\text{NO}_2$ from the exhaust gases of car engines.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Iron acts as a heterogeneous catalyst in the Haber process.

Describe the mode of action of this iron catalyst.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
$\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ions act as a homogeneous catalyst in the reaction between $\text{I}^{-}\text{(aq)}$ and $\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}\text{(aq)}$.

Write equations for the **two** reactions that occur when $\text{Fe}^{2+}\text{(aq)}$ is added to a mixture of $\text{I}^{-}\text{(aq)}$ and $\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}\text{(aq)}$.

$$\text{equation 1} \quad \text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-} + \ldots\ldots$$

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: Explain the difference between a homogeneous catalyst and a heterogeneous catalyst.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ions can be oxidised to $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ions under alkaline conditions by suitable oxidising agents.
parts.text: Iron is a transition element. Explain why iron forms stable compounds in both the +2 and the +3 oxidation states.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The half-equation for the reduction of $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ under alkaline conditions, and its $E^{\ominus}$ value, are shown.
$$\text{Fe(OH)}_3 + \text{e}^{-} \rightleftharpoons \text{Fe(OH)}_2 + \text{OH}^{-} \qquad E^{\ominus} = -0.56\text{ V}$$

Four more half-equations for reactions under alkaline conditions, and their $E^{\ominus}$ values, are shown.
$$\text{Al(OH)}_4^{-} + 3\text{e}^{-} \rightleftharpoons \text{Al} + 4\text{OH}^{-} \qquad E^{\ominus} = -2.35\text{ V}$$
$$\text{ClO}^{-} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + 2\text{e}^{-} \rightleftharpoons \text{Cl}^{-} + 2\text{OH}^{-} \qquad E^{\ominus} = +0.89\text{ V}$$
$$\text{O}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + 4\text{e}^{-} \rightleftharpoons 4\text{OH}^{-} \qquad E^{\ominus} = +0.40\text{ V}$$
$$\text{Zn(OH)}_4^{2-} + 2\text{e}^{-} \rightleftharpoons \text{Zn} + 4\text{OH}^{-} \qquad E^{\ominus} = -1.22\text{ V}$$

Select **two** oxidising agents that can oxidise $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ions to $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ions under alkaline conditions.

Write an equation, and give the $E^{\ominus}_{\text{cell}}$ value, for **each** of the **two** reactions that occur.
